claims.title: Source-fiber countermodel
claims.bounded_claim: A concrete finite source map has two distinct source values in one cut fiber. This counters source injectivity in the selected model unless a discriminating assumption is supplied; it does not assert that every actual cut has multiple sources.
assumptions: Source and Cut are bounded finite model types
The source-to-cut map is supplied as model data
Distinctness and equality are evaluated only inside the selected model
claims.authority_ceiling: The countermodel refutes only the generic inference from an accessible cut to a unique upstream source in this realization. It neither identifies an ultimate source nor establishes a universal multiplicity theorem.
claims.predecessor_or_countercase: Two distinct source constructors map to the same cut constructor, forming a checked non-singleton fiber.
claims.pal_account_status_note: Formal result records no PAL OPEN, CLOSED_IN_SCOPE, or REOPENED account-status event; D-FIRST-OCCURRENCE remains OPEN separately.

claims.title: Downstream cut congruence
claims.bounded_claim: For any supplied downstream function whose only input is Cut, equal cuts produce equal downstream results. The theorem is congruence at the declared interface and says nothing about routes with a source side channel or additional discriminating witness.
assumptions: The downstream route is represented by a pure function Cut -> Result
The compared source images are equal as Cut values
No additional source-bearing input is available to the downstream function
claims.authority_ceiling: Cut-level observational equality does not prove source identity, physical indistinguishability, or equality under richer interfaces.
claims.predecessor_or_countercase: AR2-01 supplies distinct sources with equal cut images; any Cut-only downstream function therefore receives equal inputs.
claims.pal_account_status_note: Formal result records no PAL OPEN, CLOSED_IN_SCOPE, or REOPENED account-status event; D-FIRST-OCCURRENCE remains OPEN separately.

claims.title: Occurrence does not identify source
claims.bounded_claim: The selected model simultaneously contains a later-witnessed local occurrence, makes the same occurrence structure empty when its later-witness type is NoWitness, and has a noninjective source-to-cut map. This separates bounded occurrence recovery from source identification.
assumptions: The occurrence receipt is local to a declared account
A distinct later witness and the two-instant finite activity model are supplied
The source map is the noninjective bounded model used by AR2-01
claims.authority_ceiling: The countermodel does not deny that a source exists, prove that source knowledge is impossible, or promote scoped occurrence closure into global or ontic closure.
claims.predecessor_or_countercase: The witnessed occurrence is inhabited, the corresponding NoWitness occurrence is empty, and the displayed sigma maps two distinct sources to the shared accessible cut.
claims.pal_account_status_note: Formal result records no PAL OPEN, CLOSED_IN_SCOPE, or REOPENED account-status event; D-FIRST-OCCURRENCE remains OPEN separately.

claims.predecessor_or_countercase: The bounded cost receipt is inhabited while a causal-source receipt requiring the empty witness type is uninhabited.
claims.pal_account_status_note: Formal result records no PAL OPEN, CLOSED_IN_SCOPE, or REOPENED account-status event; D-FIRST-OCCURRENCE remains OPEN separately.
